canonical_topic: California's marginal fuel and regional natural gas supply split
definition: Because natural-gas-fired plants are typically the marginal (price-setting) generators in California, the state's power prices are tied to gas supply, which comes from two distinct sources depending on region.
core_idea: Southern California draws its marginal gas supply from the Rocky Mountains and West Texas, while Northern California draws from western Canada, so a price divergence between those two gas supply basins can create corresponding divergence in regional power prices.
key_points: Natural-gas-fired plants are usually the marginal producers of power in California
Southern part of the region gets gas from the Rocky Mountains and West Texas
Northern part gets gas from western Canada
Divergent fuel prices between the two source basins can affect regional power price differentials
trading_implications: Gas basis spreads between Rockies/West Texas and western Canada are a useful signal for anticipated NP-15 vs SP-15 power price divergence
